question: Should OpenClaw core adopt Discord source-message subagent progress as a supported feature, including seven configuration fields and new shared delivery/lifecycle plugin contracts?
rationale: The implementation is proven and has no concrete correctness finding, but review cannot decide whether this permanent configuration and plugin API surface belongs in core or should be narrowed without owner intent.

options.title: Sponsor and stabilize
options.body: Approve the feature direction, explicitly own the shared lifecycle and message-origin contracts, and require an exact-main refresh with compatibility and delivery gates before merge.

options.title: Narrow the permanent surface
options.body: Keep Discord progress behavior but reduce configurable knobs and avoid published/shared lifecycle API growth where an internal generic seam is sufficient.

options.title: Decline core ownership
options.body: Leave existing Discord streaming/status behavior as the core path and move richer delegated-work presentation to an external plugin or later product initiative.

recommendation.title: Sponsor and stabilize
recommendation.body: Approve the feature direction, explicitly own the shared lifecycle and message-origin contracts, and require an exact-main refresh with compatibility and delivery gates before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The product behavior is Discord-specific, while the agents and plugin maintainers can review the shared contracts after Discord direction is confirmed.
